I will keep it simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the land, weather, and water conditions fit the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation best, and at my age I would rather choose the cropping pattern I know well and can manage reliably. I will keep most of my land in winter wheat first, because it is already the backbone crop here and I understand its fertilizer, irrigation, and disease control rhythm. After wheat harvest, I will sow summer maize right away, because it follows wheat well, uses the summer heat and rain, and gives me a second harvest from the same land. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and standability, but I will not make the management too complicated. I will apply fertilizer at moderate levels, not too little and not too much, because I want stable output and do not want to waste money. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat in our area depends more on timely water, especially at overwintering, jointing, and grain filling. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage after harvest because it is familiar and practical for me. I will spray only as needed, mainly for common wheat diseases, aphids, and maize pests, because I want to protect yield without making too many passes.
